description: Every agent of the agent-teams-workforce plugin, generated from its definition file by skills/find-specialists/scripts/specialist_catalog.py. Do not edit by hand.

agents.name: acceptance-criteria-coverage-assessor
agents.description: Establishes, before any test is written, which acceptance criteria the repository's existing tests already encode and which are gaps, and — when every criterion is covered — runs only those tests and rules whether they are red, already-satisfied or not-encoded. Use before Red to avoid duplicate tests or a manufactured red for behaviour that already exists. Never writes or repairs a test.

agents.name: acceptance-criteria-reviewer
agents.description: Reviews acceptance criteria and Definition of Done statements for testability, completeness and ambiguity: whether a test can be derived from each without interpretation, with boundary and failure cases covered; reports findings, never fixes. For a caller that wants criteria checked on their own; in elaboration spec-reviewer reviews the criteria document with the specs.

agents.name: acceptance-criteria-writer
agents.description: Derive traceable criteria and Definition of Done from the finished specification set.

agents.name: accessibility-validator
agents.description: Validates UI changes against WCAG 2.2 A/AA — contrast, keyboard navigation, ARIA, focus management, screen-reader flows — reporting violations with locations and remediations; never fixes. Use for Code Quality work requiring WCAG validation, accessibility regression detection, and focus-order review.

agents.name: advantage-evaluator
agents.description: Rules commit or revert on a competitive (non-constitutive) finding that work was allowed to proceed under: before the outcome exists it states the observation window and the evidence that will decide, then judges the observed outcome against it. Speculative execution with rollback, so a tradeable finding never halts a run. Use when a caller proceeded past a competitive gate flag or a non-blocking concern and needs it closed on evidence.

agents.name: adversarial-critique-adjudicator
agents.description: Rules on each adversarial finding whether it is real, its severity, and whether it is constitutive (a hard stop) or competitive (a tradeable concern), with a rationale per finding; the referee whose rulings implementers cannot downgrade. Use for Adversarial Validation phase work requiring finding adjudication and constitutive-vs-competitive classification.

agents.name: adversarial-review-loop-supervisor
agents.description: Sequences the adversarial validation loop: testers attack project code in designated test environments only; the Adversarial Critique Adjudicator rules on findings, which route back until pass or loop-limit escalation. Use for Adversarial Validation phase work requiring attack-wave orchestration, finding routing, and loop-limit enforcement.

agents.name: ai-agent-designer
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on custom AI agents - Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime and Harness, agent frameworks such as Strands, AgentCore Memory, tools through AgentCore Gateway and MCP, multi-agent and A2A, AgentCore Identity and Cedar policies, and agent bounds.

agents.name: ambiguity-detector
agents.description: Finds the requirements of a PRD whose user-observable behavior is unclear, contradictory within itself or open to two incompatible readings (vague quantifiers, missing user-observable boundary conditions, unstated assumptions); reports each with a concrete clarification, never fixes. Use for the ambiguity lens of PRD validation.

agents.name: analytics-query-designer
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on serverless SQL analytics with Amazon Athena over the data lake — workgroups and their limits, query result handling, data layout for scan cost, partition projection, federated and Iceberg queries, CTAS and UNLOAD, and capacity.

agents.name: android-compose-implementer
agents.description: Implements Android features in Kotlin and Jetpack Compose; writes minimum code to pass failing Espresso suites. Use for Implementation work requiring Compose UI, Kotlin state and navigation wiring, and on-device ML Kit integration.

agents.name: api-contract-designer
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on REST APIs on Amazon API Gateway (REST API): which building block exposes each interface, its resources and methods, who may call it and how the caller is authorized, request validation, throttling and usage plans, errors, and how it stays compatible.

agents.name: api-documentation-writer
agents.description: Updates the human-readable API reference documents of shipped APIs from their OpenAPI and GraphQL specifications: endpoint and operation guides, request, response and error examples, SDK snippets. Never edits a specification file.

agents.name: api-gateway-cdk-implementer
agents.description: Implements API Gateway resources, methods, and authorizers in CDK; writes minimum code to pass failing unit tests. Use for Implementation work requiring API Gateway constructs, CDK infrastructure, and authorizer wiring.

agents.name: api-specification-author
agents.description: Write the spec of the API, event, error and UI contracts one repository's Story builds, from the recorded architecture and design; designs nothing.

agents.name: applied-ai-services-designer
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on the AWS pre-trained AI services - Amazon Textract document extraction, Amazon Rekognition image and video analysis, and Amazon Comprehend text analysis and PII detection - their operations, synchronous or asynchronous paths, limits, confidence handling and cost.

agents.name: appsync-cdk-implementer
agents.description: Implements AppSync GraphQL APIs in CDK: schema wiring, resolvers, data sources, authorization. Use for Implementation work requiring AppSync API construction, resolver and data source wiring, and authorization setup.

agents.name: appsync-client-subscription-implementer
agents.description: Implements AppSync client subscriptions for real-time web features. Use for Implementation work requiring GraphQL subscription wiring, connection lifecycle handling, real-time state updates, and reconnection handling.

agents.name: architecture-boundary-guardian
agents.description: Review, for the solutions architect, the boundaries of a design: whether each building block's responsibilities and owned data stay inside its bounded context, whether every interface that crosses a boundary is explicit about who exposes it and who may call it, whether shared behaviour is taken from its shared home, and whether the design breaks a section 2 constraint or departs from an established pattern without a stated reason.

agents.name: architecture-conformance-reviewer
agents.description: Check, without modifying anything, that a correction of the effective architecture documents describes each element exactly as the built views of a Story record it, at every scope, with conforming front matter and placement and section 2 untouched.

agents.name: architecture-decider
agents.description: Rule between the positions on an architecture matter the solutions architect and the architecture team lead could not settle, from the evidence each position carries, and record the ruling in the matrix as the settlement of the disagreement.

agents.name: architecture-diagram-author
agents.description: Draw one architecture diagram of a design the solutions architect has settled, of any view type the documentation model lists (C4, UML, context map, data flow, deployment and the others), and return it with its home, view type and the elements it shows.

agents.name: architecture-fitness-function-author
agents.description: Defines testable assertions from the owner's constraints and the architecture decisions, e.g. "every Lambda uses the configured logging library", "no service reads another service's table". Use for Architecture Analysis work requiring fitness function authoring, constraint formalization, and conformance criteria.

agents.name: architecture-impact-analyst
agents.description: Judges what an architecture change reaches. Given the architecture views an integration changed, created or deleted, it takes from the matrix every Epic, open Task and entry those views reach (`atw-matrix impact`, `affected`), and rules on each one: unaffected, not yet elaborated, elaborated but unbuilt, or already built, with a knock-on Task proposed for each built item. It changes no bead and writes no code or document; it writes only its result file. Use after an architecture change created, changed or retired architecture views.

agents.name: architecture-maintainer
agents.description: Write the solutions architect's decisions into the architecture documents (arc42 and detailed/), each fact in its one home with links from every other document, and correct the effective documents to match what a Story built.

agents.name: architecture-pattern-challenger
agents.description: Review, for the solutions architect, the structure of a design for concrete weaknesses: a mechanism that does not do what the requirement needs, a structure more complex than the requirement, or an AWS pattern used against its documented best practice, each reported with the simpler sufficient repair.

agents.name: architecture-team-lead
agents.description: Route what the solutions architect could not settle, so that the team settles it with the least further work.

agents.name: architecture-tradeoff-skeptic
agents.description: Review, for the solutions architect, the trade-off claims of a design: whether each choice between options states the options and a reason the evidence supports, and whether the assumptions and estimates it rests on (latency, throughput, limits, effort) hold against the stated constraints and AWS documentation.

agents.name: athena-redshift-analytics-implementer
agents.description: Implements Athena queries and Redshift analytics models over the data lake — tables, views, SQL — writing minimum code to pass failing data-pipeline tests. Use for Implementation work requiring analytics SQL authoring, external table definition, and warehouse modeling.

agents.name: audit-and-compliance-designer
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on AWS CloudTrail (trails, management and data events, CloudTrail Lake, log integrity and retention) and AWS Config (recording, managed and custom rules, conformance packs, remediation), and the Security Hub controls they feed.

agents.name: auth-bypass-tester
agents.description: Attempts auth bypass — token forgery, session fixation, flow skipping — against the project's auth flows in designated test environments only, reporting each confirmed bypass. Use for Adversarial Validation phase work requiring auth-flow attack, Cognito probing, and minimal-reproduction reporting.

agents.name: aws-integration-test-runner
agents.description: Runs AWS integration test suites against the provisioned test environment, reporting structured pass/fail, coverage, and flakiness results. Use for Integration Testing work requiring suite execution, coverage measurement, and flakiness detection.

agents.name: aws-integration-test-writer
agents.description: Writes failing integration tests covering the event delivery path the effective architecture describes, hop by hop. Use for Test Design work requiring AWS integration test authoring, event-driven flow assertions, and test harness design.

agents.name: aws-solutions-architect
agents.description: Hold single responsibility for the architecture a PRD needs, from the first read of the PRD until the architecture and the TRD are designed, reviewed and approved, with the review log that proves how.

agents.name: batch-compute-designer
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on AWS Batch: compute environments (Fargate, EC2, Spot), job queues and their priorities, job definitions, array and multi-node jobs, retries and timeouts, and scheduling policies.

agents.name: beads-format-validator
agents.description: Validates that Beads issues are structurally complete (title, acceptance criteria found where the beads contract looks, dependencies that resolve, spec links that resolve) and obey the hierarchy rule; reports defects, never fixes. For a caller that wants a set of issues checked before work starts.

agents.name: bedrock-integration-implementer
agents.description: Implements the code that calls Amazon Bedrock foundation models - Converse and ConverseStream calls, prompt assembly from specified templates, guardrail and prompt-cache settings on the call, structured-output parsing, and inference error handling - writing minimum code to pass failing tests. Embeddings calls belong to vector-search-embeddings-implementer.

agents.name: behavioral-signals-implementer
agents.description: Implements behavioral signal capture and feature pipelines feeding matching and recommendation models; minimum code to pass failing tests. Use for Implementation work requiring event signal capture, feature engineering, and ML feature delivery.

agents.name: block-and-file-storage-designer
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on block and file storage for EC2, containers and Lambda on Amazon EBS, Amazon EFS and Amazon FSx (Lustre, NetApp ONTAP, OpenZFS, Windows File Server) — volume and file system type, performance and throughput mode, availability, snapshots and backups, lifecycle tiering and access.

agents.name: bounded-context-mapper
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on bounded contexts: their boundaries, domain responsibilities, which service owns each, the relationships between contexts and the published language each exposes.

agents.name: brd-traceability-auditor
agents.description: Maps each PRD requirement to the objectives of a BRD the run names, for information only: a correspondence, never a verdict on the PRD. Use for the informational BRD traceability lens of PRD validation.

agents.name: built-architecture-comparer
agents.description: Compare the code one Story built with the approved architecture and design headings that describe the stacks and entries it built, and record each difference as an in-review view under built/<element>/, citing the code by file and line.

agents.name: c4-diagram-author
agents.description: Draw one C4 diagram (system context, container, component or deployment) of a design the solutions architect has settled, and return it with its home, view type and the elements it shows.

agents.name: cache-designer
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on in-memory caching and in-memory data stores on Amazon ElastiCache (Valkey, Redis OSS, Memcached; serverless or node-based) and Amazon MemoryDB — caching pattern, key and TTL design, invalidation, eviction, topology, durability and multi-Region replication.

agents.name: cdk-infrastructure-designer
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on which repository and which CDK stack hold each resource and building block, how stacks share values, which shared infrastructure must exist first, and construct and parameter names; and express the infrastructure the architecture records for a build Task as CDK provisioning intent.

agents.name: cdk-infrastructure-drift-detector
agents.description: Detects drift between a repository's deployed CloudFormation stacks and its CDK app (cdk diff, CloudFormation drift detection, template comparison) and reports each divergence with evidence; read-only, never remediates. A specialist a caller chooses to check deployed infrastructure against its code.

agents.name: cdk-stack-author
agents.description: Writes AWS CDK stacks, constructs and app wiring in Python for an infrastructure Task, as the Task, its spec, the provisioning intent and the architecture give them, with the minimum change that makes the failing synth assertion tests pass. Never deploys.

agents.name: cds-finding-reviewer
agents.description: Rules on the findings a deterministic cds audit of a Task's changed UI could not rule on - each class name the supplied cds bundle's stylesheets do not name - as a violation, allowed, or a cds gap, against the bundle and the configured design system; changes no file.

agents.name: cds-live-auditor
agents.description: Audits the UI files a Task changed against the live Configurable Design System (cds) when no mockup or cds bundle was supplied, and rules each finding.

agents.name: cds-ui-implementer
agents.description: Implements a Task's web UI components and pages in the application repository with the Configurable Design System (cds) applied by construction, from the supplied cds bundle or the live design system, and audits the changed UI against it before reporting; writes the minimum code that makes the failing tests pass.

agents.name: changed-resource-cost-reviewer
agents.description: Review, for the solutions architect, the cost effect of a design's changes to existing resources: changed billable limits, capacity modes, retention or usage, the cost assumptions each change rests on, a monthly floor it adds or moves, and any cost cliff (a pricing tier, free-tier limit, quota or capacity-mode boundary) the stated usage reaches.

agents.name: changelog-writer
agents.description: Writes the changelog entries for a change before it merges, from the change and the conventional commits on its branch, in the project's changelog format, flagging breaking changes and recommending the semantic version increment. Never decides, sets or bumps a version.

agents.name: chassis-extension-implementer
agents.description: Implements Lambda handlers as chassis superclass extensions for API endpoints and event consumers; writes minimum code to pass failing unit tests. Use for Implementation work requiring Lambda handlers, chassis extension, and endpoint/consumer business logic.

agents.name: code-correctness-reviewer
agents.description: Independently reviews a refactor or optimisation change set for correctness regressions and behavioral drift: re-runs the test suite itself, compares contracts, error and data semantics and side effects before and after, and flags modified, weakened or skipped tests and suppressed lint rules; reports findings, never fixes. Use when a caller wants an independent behaviour-preservation check of a change set.

agents.name: code-quality-lead
agents.description: Routes refactor work to specialists, verifies tests stay green after every change, and assembles the refactor evidence packet. Use for Code Quality work requiring delegation, refactor sequencing and green-test verification.

agents.name: code-refactoring-specialist
agents.description: Refactors the code a change touched for clarity, cohesion, less complexity and less duplication without changing behavior: decides which refactorings the changed files need (none is a valid answer), applies them through GitNexus (impact before each symbol, rename for every rename, detect_changes before finishing), and keeps the test suite green or gives up so the caller restores the tree.

agents.name: cognito-lambda-trigger-implementer
agents.description: Implements Cognito Lambda triggers — sign-up, confirmation, token customization, custom auth challenges — on the chassis the architecture describes. Use for Implementation work requiring Cognito trigger logic, auth flows, and user pool event processing.

agents.name: completeness-checker
agents.description: Checks that each requirement of a PRD has an actor, a trigger or action, an observable user outcome and a behavioral acceptance criterion, and reports each missing or defective element; never supplies one. Use for the completeness lens of PRD validation.

agents.name: complexity-analyzer
agents.description: Analyzes complexity and duplication in a green-tested change set and returns a prioritized refactor recommendation memo, with the optimizer specialties (Lambda, DynamoDB cost, front-end performance, lint fixing) the change calls for; performs no refactoring. Use when a caller wants refactoring targeted by evidence before it assigns the work.

agents.name: constitutional-agent
agents.description: Rules on a conflict between two constitutive constraints that no gate can settle: establishes the constitutional layer the conflict falls under (the owner's section 2 constraints and settled decisions recorded in the matrix, the business outcomes of the PRD the work serves, and the review standard's acceptance basis), names which constraint prevails and under what conditions, and writes the ruling as a precedent record a later conflict can cite. Use when two constraints that each define validity cannot both be met.

agents.name: constraint-extractor
agents.description: Extracts the explicit and implied constraints a PRD imposes (regulatory, business, platform, policy), each with its kind and where the PRD states or implies it; invents none. Use for the constraints lens of PRD validation.

agents.name: consumer-driven-contract-test-writer
agents.description: Writes failing consumer-driven contract tests from the spec's API and event contracts. Use for Test Design work requiring contract test authoring, consumer expectation modeling, and provider verification setup.

agents.name: container-service-designer
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on containers on Amazon ECS: Fargate or ECS Managed Instances or EC2 capacity, task definitions (CPU, memory, containers, health checks), services and their deployment and scaling, Amazon ECR repositories and image lifecycle.

agents.name: context-curator
agents.description: Assembles a context index for one receiving agent and task: a file of pointers (paths, headings, matrix ids and atw-matrix commands) to exactly what the role needs, with every constitutive constraint that binds it carried by pointer to its one home, never copied or summarized, and keeps the constraint manifest those pointers come from current. Use when starting a session by hand that needs its context assembled under least context; the orchestrator's own briefs already carry paths only.

agents.name: contract-violation-tester
agents.description: Sends contract-violating inputs — malformed payloads, type/range violations, schema mismatches — across the project's service boundaries in designated test environments only. Use for Adversarial Validation phase work requiring contract-boundary attack, API/event schema probing, and minimal-reproduction reporting.

agents.name: cross-repo-integration-test-coordinator
agents.description: Sequences cross-repo integration test runs over the event chain, aligns environment state between repos, and routes consolidated results to its caller. Coordinates only — runs no tests. Use for Integration Testing work requiring cross-repo sequencing, environment alignment, and result routing.

agents.name: cross-service-contract-tester
agents.description: Runs contract tests across service and repo boundaries, verifying providers and consumers honor approved API and event contracts. Use for Integration Testing work requiring consumer-driven contract verification, schema compatibility checks, and cross-repo boundary testing.

agents.name: data-architect
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on pure data architecture independent of any engine — conceptual and logical data models, entities and relationships, which domain owns each entity and its system of record, data flows and lineage, reference and master data, data classification and retention classes, operational versus analytical data, and data contracts between domains.

agents.name: data-consistency-checker
agents.description: Verifies data consistency across services and stores after integration and event-flow runs — partial writes, orphaned records, divergent state. Use for Integration Testing work requiring cross-store verification, DynamoDB assertions, and eventual-consistency validation.

agents.name: data-exposure-scanner
agents.description: Scans the project's responses, logs, and storage in designated test environments only for data exposure — leaked secrets, PII, over-returned fields, unencrypted storage — reporting each confirmed exposure. Use for Adversarial Validation phase work requiring data-leak scanning, secret/PII detection, and minimal-reproduction reporting.

agents.name: data-lake-designer
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on the data lake on AWS Glue, AWS Lake Formation and Amazon S3 Tables — zones and table layout, open table format (Apache Iceberg), partitioning, the Glue Data Catalog, ingestion and ETL jobs, connections to sources, data quality and Lake Formation permissions.

agents.name: data-model-specification-author
agents.description: Write the spec of the data one repository's Story builds, from the recorded architecture and design; designs nothing.

agents.name: data-pipeline-test-writer
agents.description: Writes failing data pipeline tests — ETL correctness, CDC ordering, data quality, replay safety — confirming each fails for the intended reason. Use for Test Design work requiring pipeline test authoring, data quality assertions, and replay-safety checks.

agents.name: data-warehouse-designer
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on data warehousing on Amazon Redshift (Serverless or provisioned RA3) — workgroup or cluster shape, table design (distribution, sort keys, encoding), loading with COPY and zero-ETL, materialized views, data sharing, Spectrum and workload management.

agents.name: definition-of-done-writer
agents.description: Writes the Definition of Done of a given scope of work as independently verifiable true-or-false statements about the finished work, never checklist steps, each traced to the requirement or design decision it comes from. For a caller that needs a Definition of Done on its own; in elaboration the acceptance-criteria-writer writes it with the criteria.

agents.name: dependency-change-detector
agents.description: Detects dependency version and contract changes since a specification was written, by diffing manifests and lockfiles against the spec-time reference and checking changed contracts, classing each as unchanged, reconciled in the spec, or needing reconciliation. For a caller that holds a spec written some time before its build.

agents.name: dependency-cve-auditor
agents.description: Audits the project's Python and Node dependencies for known CVEs, scoring severity and exploitable transitive paths. Use for Adversarial Validation phase work requiring CVE scanning, severity scoring, and supply-chain risk reporting.

agents.name: deploy-failure-fixer
agents.description: Diagnoses a failed package publish, cdk synth, cdk deploy to AWS dev or stack verification from its output and the CloudFormation stack events, fixes the CDK (or whatever else the deploy needs) in the Story's worktree, runs the repository's synth assertion tests, corrects a test the fix proves wrong, and names the command that runs them. Never deploys, commits or publishes.

agents.name: deployment-lead
agents.description: Routes the feature deployment sequence, validates preconditions per step, and assembles the deployment evidence packet. Use for Deployment team work requiring delegation, sequencing discipline, and evidence assembly.

agents.name: deployment-strategy-decider
agents.description: Decides one repository's deployment strategy (rollout mechanism such as Lambda alias traffic shifting, canary, blue-green or all-at-once; canary health criteria; rollback triggers) from analyses others produced (rollout options and risk, FinOps, SLO design, drift), with a recorded rationale; produces no analysis. A specialist a caller chooses when a rollout must be decided.

agents.name: dev-deployer
agents.description: Deploys one repository to AWS dev by the mechanism the repository deploys by (cdk deploy of the affected stacks, or the repository's own deploy path such as a static-site build, S3 sync and CloudFront invalidation), then runs its smoke tests or names the one command that runs them. Never deploys to any other environment and never writes code.

agents.name: developer-documentation-writer
agents.description: Updates a repository's internal and technical documents so they match the shipped code: developer guides, design and implementation notes, module and service documentation, configuration references and contributing guides. Not READMEs, changelogs, API reference documents, user guides or specification files.

agents.name: dns-and-edge-designer
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on Amazon Route 53 and Amazon CloudFront: hosted zones, records and routing policies, health checks and failover, CloudFront distributions, origins and origin access control, cache and origin request policies, edge functions, and custom domains.

agents.name: document-database-designer
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on document data on Amazon DocumentDB (MongoDB compatible) — cluster type and capacity, document model (embedding or referencing), indexes, MongoDB API compatibility, change streams, transactions and read scaling.

agents.name: documentation-accuracy-reviewer
agents.description: Reviews the documents a documentation writer updated for a change against the behaviour the change ships, claim by claim, and reports each inaccurate claim and each uncovered behaviour with cited evidence. Read-only; never fixes.

agents.name: documentation-currency-auditor
agents.description: Audits which documents a change leaves stale or missing, with cited evidence, and assigns each stale document to the documentation writer whose kind covers it (API reference, README, changelog, user guide, or internal and technical documents); names the specification files the change contradicts. Read-only.

agents.name: documentation-lead
agents.description: Routes documentation work for shipped changes, tracks artifacts lacking current docs, and reports documentation currency. Use for cross-cutting Documentation team work requiring delegation, currency tracking, and currency reporting.

agents.name: domain-boundary-validator
agents.description: Checks that a PRD's requirements stay inside one bounded context, and reports each requirement that makes the feature own behavior another feature or service owns or that sits in more than one context. Use for the domain-boundary lens of PRD validation.

agents.name: domain-event-modeler
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on domain events as facts: which fact each event states, the bounded context and aggregate that owns it, what triggers it, the causal flow it belongs to and the business meaning of the data it carries.

agents.name: dos-resilience-tester
agents.description: Probes load and resource-exhaustion resilience in designated test environments only, reporting where throttling, backpressure, or quotas fail; findings are competitive, not gate-stopping. Use for Adversarial Validation phase work requiring exhaustion probing, resilience evaluation, and competitive-finding reporting.

agents.name: dynamodb-access-layer-implementer
agents.description: Implements DynamoDB access patterns from the data model spec; writes minimum code to pass failing tests. Use for Implementation work requiring single-table design, GSI query construction, and conditional write semantics.

agents.name: dynamodb-cost-optimizer
agents.description: Reduces the DynamoDB cost of code whose tests are green within the approved data model — scans replaced by keyed queries, batching, projections, pagination, fewer round trips — and recommends capacity-mode and index changes with a stated cost basis, without changing behavior or data semantics. Use when a caller assigns DynamoDB cost items.

agents.name: dynamodb-schema-access-pattern-reviewer
agents.description: Reviews the DynamoDB stores of one repository's data-model spec: whether each access pattern it states can be served by the keys and indexes it states, at the stated capacity, without a scan or client-side filtering, and whether each store has the key attributes, indexes, access patterns and expiry attribute the detailed design records. Returns findings the data-model author can correct without interpretation; changes nothing.

agents.name: dynamodb-streams-cdc-implementer
agents.description: Implements change data capture from DynamoDB Streams; writes minimum code to pass failing data-pipeline test suites. Use for Implementation work requiring stream record processing, change event transformation, and exactly-once-effect handling.

agents.name: dynamodb-table-designer
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on Amazon DynamoDB and DAX — access-pattern-first single-table or multi-table design, partition and sort keys, GSIs and LSIs, capacity mode, TTL, streams, transactions, global tables, backups and cost.

agents.name: ec2-fleet-designer
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on Amazon EC2 fleets: instance type selection, AMIs, launch templates, Auto Scaling groups and their scaling policies, Spot and mixed instances, IMDSv2 and fleet operations through Systems Manager.

agents.name: email-notification-implementer
agents.description: Implements transactional and notification email features: responsive templates, rendering pipelines, delivery through Amazon SES, and bounce/complaint handling. Use for Implementation work requiring email template construction and delivery wiring.

agents.name: encryption-and-secrets-designer
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on AWS KMS keys and key policies, envelope encryption and key rotation, AWS Secrets Manager secrets and their rotation, and AWS Certificate Manager certificates.

agents.name: epic-dependency-assessor
agents.description: Proposes and validates the architecture-dependency edges to and from ONE Epic, by the edge test of the epic-sequencing skill, and accounts for every owned edge standing on it; orders nothing, scores nothing and applies nothing.

agents.name: espresso-test-writer
agents.description: Writes failing Espresso suites for Android features from spec acceptance criteria, confirming each test fails for the intended reason. Use for Test Design work requiring Espresso authoring, Android UI coverage, Compose semantics matchers, and Red confirmation.

agents.name: event-api-client-implementer
agents.description: Implements the calls a service makes to the project's central event API to publish the project's events. Use for Implementation work requiring event publishing calls, mapping of domain values to the API request, and event contract conformance.

agents.name: event-driven-consumer-implementer
agents.description: Implements the handler code of a routing rule's target, for whatever target type the target's owner chose. Use for Implementation work requiring event handler logic, batch processing where the target delivers batches, and reading of the project's standard event.

agents.name: event-flow-tester
agents.description: Tests event flows end-to-end through the EventBridge-SQS-Lambda chain, verifying delivery, routing, retry, and dead-letter behavior per hop. Use for Integration Testing work requiring event-driven flow validation, EventBridge rule verification, and queue/consumer checks.

agents.name: event-routing-designer
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on Amazon EventBridge: event type names and their registry entries, the payload schema of a new event type, buses, routing rules (event pattern, targets, owning stack), each rule target's retry policy and dead-letter queue, and EventBridge Scheduler schedules.

agents.name: event-schema-reviewer
agents.description: Validates event contracts against the project's standard event and each event's payload schema — event type names, passed values, publishing conditions, consumer obligations, retry/DLQ behavior. Use for Spec Authoring work requiring standard-event conformance, event contract validation, and failure-semantics checks.

agents.name: exhausted-gate-ruler
agents.description: Rules how a run continues from a phase gate whose loops are spent: proceed, with the latest output standing and every unmet criterion carried on as a named residual with its mitigation, or one directed revision under a concrete, changed instruction. Started by the gate-enforce workflow in its exhaustion mode.

agents.name: failure-mode-analyst
agents.description: Review, for the solutions architect, how a design fails and recovers: throttling, duplicate and out-of-order delivery, poison messages, downstream outages, timeouts, retries, dead-letter queues, idempotency and recovery paths across Lambda, SQS, SNS, EventBridge and the event path, as the runtime views and the TRD state them.

agents.name: feature-objective-writer
agents.description: Writes the one objective a feature must move and the key results that prove it was met, grounded in the feature's intake: a qualitative, user-centered objective and measurable key results, each with its metric and target. Use as the objective step of PRD creation.

agents.name: feature-persona-writer
agents.description: Writes the one target persona a feature serves, grounded in the audience, problem and outcome of the feature's intake: a proto-persona whose goals, frustrations and context are each stated, inferred or marked as an assumption, behavior over demographics. Use as the persona step of PRD creation.

agents.name: filing-clerk
agents.description: The documentation filing clerk for the SkillSpoke knowledge base. Hand it a fact, decision, definition, or note and it (1) searches the skillspoke-docs Obsidian vault — fast, from several angles — to see whether it is already documented, (2) hunts for any single-source-of-truth violation (an unmarked duplicate of something canonical), (3) if the fact is genuinely new, decides the one correct home and files it there with proper classification frontmatter, and (4) reports what it did and any conflicts for the owner to adjudicate. Use PROACTIVELY whenever the owner says things like "if we don't have it already, note that…", "file this", "document that…", "make sure it's written down somewhere", "capture this", "record that we decided…", "add … to arc42 / the glossary / the docs", or offloads a fact so the owner won't forget it. Examples: "note in arc42 somewhere that we use Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and the Strands Agents SDK for our agent" → clerk checks the SAD, files under §4 Solution Strategy if absent; "define 'aging authority' in the glossary if it isn't there" → clerk searches, adds a glossary term; "record that student verification uses SheerID" → clerk finds the right tech/spec doc and files it.

agents.name: finops-analyst
agents.description: Models what a feature costs to run on AWS before it ships — unit economics, scaling cost curves across load scenarios, budget impact, cost cliffs — and ranks cost recommendations; decides nothing. A specialist a caller chooses for a pre-deployment cost analysis.

agents.name: flaky-test-detector
agents.description: Verifies intermittent test failures via repeated controlled reruns; reports verified-flaky tests as findings only — never edits or disables tests. Use for Integration Testing work requiring flakiness verification, rerun-based reproduction, and root-cause findings.

agents.name: foundation-model-designer
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on Amazon Bedrock foundation models - model and inference profile choice per task, Converse API calls, maxTokens and timeouts, quotas and throughput, prompt caching, attaching guardrails to a model call, and inference cost.

agents.name: frontend-performance-optimizer
agents.description: Applies measured frontend performance optimizations — bundle trimming, code splitting and lazy loading, render-path fixes, Core Web Vitals (LCP, INP, CLS) — to React and Next.js code whose tests are green, without changing behavior, accessibility or visual output. Use when a caller assigns frontend performance items.

agents.name: generative-ai-pattern-designer
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on generative AI flow patterns - prompt chaining, routing, parallelisation, orchestrator and workers, evaluator-optimiser loops, prompt structure, structured output, chain of verification, LLM-as-judge evaluation, human in the loop and applying guardrails to a flow.

agents.name: github-actions-pipeline-implementer
agents.description: Writes and changes a repository's GitHub Actions workflows: OIDC authentication to AWS with no stored credentials, dependency and build caching, and the build, test, lint and deploy jobs the repository's own commands define. A specialist a caller chooses when a repository's CI/CD workflows must be created or changed.

agents.name: glue-etl-implementer
agents.description: Implements Glue ETL jobs for batch data processing; writes minimum code to pass failing data-pipeline suites. Use for Implementation work requiring Glue job authoring, PySpark transformations, and batch pipeline construction.

agents.name: graph-database-designer
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on graph data on Amazon Neptune Database and Neptune Analytics — engine and capacity choice, property graph or RDF, node and edge model, query language (openCypher, Gremlin, SPARQL), traversal and supernode design, loading, graph algorithms and vector search.

agents.name: graphql-api-designer
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on GraphQL APIs on AWS AppSync: schema, operations and types, which block resolves each field from which owned data, resolvers and data sources, authorization modes, subscriptions, caching and compatibility.

agents.name: graphql-schema-reviewer
agents.description: Reviews the GraphQL contracts of a specification against the architecture and detailed design that record the API and against AppSync patterns: types, operations, resolver and data-source mappings, authorization modes and directives, error shapes, pagination and naming; reports findings, never fixes. For a caller that wants a spec's GraphQL contracts checked.

agents.name: iam-policy-designer
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on AWS IAM: roles and their trust policies, identity and resource policies with least privilege, condition keys and confused-deputy protection, permission boundaries, cross-account access, service-linked and service roles, and IAM Identity Center for human access.

agents.name: implementation-lead
agents.description: Selects the implementer(s) whose specialties cover a Task, in build order, from the Task's build contract — its spec documents and the architecture views it was designed against. Use for Implementation work requiring implementer selection.

agents.name: incident-response-runbook-designer
agents.description: Writes a deployed feature's operational runbooks — incident response keyed to its alarms and SLIs, rollback steps that match its deployment strategy, and disaster recovery (backup, restore, failover) for its AWS resources — with every referenced command and resource verified. A specialist a caller chooses when a feature needs runbooks.

agents.name: infrastructure-security-scanner
agents.description: Scans project IaC and deployed test infrastructure, designated test environments only, for public exposure, over-broad IAM, missing encryption, and open security groups, reporting each with a minimal reproduction. Use for Adversarial Validation phase work requiring IaC security scanning, CDK and cloud-config review, and misconfiguration reporting.

agents.name: injection-attack-tester
agents.description: Probes this project's endpoints in designated test environments only for SQL, NoSQL, command, and template injection; reports each confirmed path with a minimal reproduction. Use for Adversarial Validation phase work requiring injection probing and input-boundary attack.

agents.name: integration-pattern-architect
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on how building blocks interact: which interactions are synchronous calls and which are events, the delivery path each takes (direct call, EventBridge rule, SNS fan-out, SQS buffer, Step Functions), and its end- to-end delivery guarantee, ordering, idempotency and failure behaviour.

agents.name: integration-testing-lead
agents.description: Read-only selector a caller invokes to choose the integration suites for a change when it cannot derive them from declared contract surfaces. Chooses the fewest applicable suites and whether provisioning must precede them, returning suites, provisionEnv and rationale. Does not dispatch workers, run tests, aggregate results, classify failures or judge gates.

agents.name: ios-swiftui-implementer
agents.description: Implements iOS features in SwiftUI; writes minimum code to pass failing XCUITest suites. Use for Implementation work requiring SwiftUI views, StoreKit purchase flows, on-device CoreML integration, and passkey/WebAuthn client wiring.

agents.name: kinesis-stream-implementer
agents.description: Implements Kinesis stream producers and consumers — record serialization, partition keys, checkpointing — writing minimum code to pass failing data-pipeline tests. Use for Implementation work requiring stream producer authoring, consumer logic, and event contract adherence.

agents.name: kubernetes-cluster-designer
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on Amazon EKS: cluster version and access, compute (managed node groups, Karpenter, Fargate profiles, EKS Auto Mode), pod networking, workload identity, add-ons and pod scaling.

agents.name: lambda-function-designer
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on AWS Lambda functions: runtime and architecture, memory, timeout and ephemeral storage, concurrency (reserved and provisioned), SnapStart, layers, invocation model and event source mappings, asynchronous invocation destinations, VPC attachment and cold-start behaviour.

agents.name: lambda-performance-optimizer
agents.description: Applies measured Lambda performance optimizations — cold start (init work, imports, bundle size), client and connection reuse, hot paths — to Lambda code whose tests are green, and recommends memory and timeout values with evidence, without changing behavior. Use when a caller assigns Lambda performance items.

agents.name: lint-finding-fixer
agents.description: Fixes the lint, format and type-check findings of a check report on a change set with the smallest style-level change, keeping tests green; never suppresses or reconfigures a rule. Use when a caller has a check report (a check runner's output or a hook's findings) whose findings must be fixed.

agents.name: llm-observability-implementer
agents.description: Implements LLM observability — prompt/response logging, token and cost metrics, drift alerts — writing minimum code to pass failing tests. Use for Implementation work requiring LLM telemetry instrumentation, quality-signal capture, and drift alerting.

agents.name: load-balancer-designer
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on Elastic Load Balancing: choosing an Application, Network or Gateway Load Balancer, listeners and TLS, routing rules, target groups and health checks, stickiness, deregistration and cross-zone behaviour.

agents.name: matching-algorithm-implementer
agents.description: Implements matching algorithms - scoring functions, ranking and tie-breaking, candidate filtering, score normalisation and the composition of these stages into the specified matcher - writing minimum code to pass failing tests. Use for Implementation work requiring matching logic and scoring and ranking functions.

agents.name: mcp-server-implementer
agents.description: Implements MCP servers on AWS, including AgentCore Gateway-fronted deployments — tool definitions and schemas, authorization, transport config, CDK deployment wiring. Use for Implementation work requiring MCP tool definitions, gateway-fronted deployments, and CDK wiring.

agents.name: ml-evaluation-tester
agents.description: Writes and runs ML evaluation suites — matching quality, recommendation relevance, embedding drift — confirming each fails before the component exists. Use for Test Design work requiring ML evaluation design, metric/threshold encoding, dataset construction, and drift detection.

agents.name: ml-feature-pipeline-designer
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on machine learning features - feature definitions and engineering, batch or streaming computation, SageMaker Feature Store online and offline stores, SageMaker Data Wrangler data preparation, training-serving consistency and feature drift.

agents.name: ml-inference-designer
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on serving trained models on Amazon SageMaker AI - real-time, serverless and asynchronous endpoints, batch transform, multi-model and multi-container endpoints, scaling, deployment guardrails and shadow tests, and Model Monitor.

agents.name: ml-training-designer
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on training and fine-tuning models on Amazon SageMaker AI - base model and technique (SFT, DPO, RLVR, RLAIF), training data, training jobs, managed Spot and checkpointing, hyperparameter tuning, evaluation and acceptance, experiment tracking and retraining.

agents.name: mobile-e2e-test-writer
agents.description: Writes failing Detox and Maestro E2E tests for React Native and cross-platform mobile flows before implementation, confirming each fails for the intended reason. Use for Test Design work requiring mobile E2E authoring, Detox and Maestro scripting, and Red confirmation.

agents.name: monitoring-and-tracing-designer
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on Amazon CloudWatch and AWS X-Ray: metrics and embedded metric format, log groups and retention, Logs Insights queries, alarms (metric, composite, anomaly detection) and their actions, dashboards, distributed tracing with X-Ray and ADOT, Application Signals, synthetics and SLO alarms.

agents.name: new-resource-cost-reviewer
agents.description: Review, for the solutions architect, the cost of each billable AWS resource a design adds: its unit prices from the AWS Price List, the monthly unit math at the stated usage computed by script, its fixed monthly floor separated from its usage cost, and the total against the stated cost ceilings.

agents.name: nextjs-component-implementer
agents.description: Implements the non-visual React/Next.js work — component state, data fetching, Next.js routing — writing minimum code to pass failing unit tests. Visual component and page work goes to cds-ui-implementer, which builds with the cds design system.

agents.name: nfr-analyst
agents.description: Lists the non-functional quality intents a PRD states or implies (performance, availability, security, privacy, accessibility, operability and the rest), each tied to the requirements that state or imply it, as input to a TRD; never quantifies them and never reports them as defects of the PRD. Available to a caller that chooses it; no workflow dispatches it.

agents.name: object-storage-designer
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on object storage on Amazon S3 and the S3 Glacier storage classes — buckets, key layout, storage classes and lifecycle, versioning and Object Lock, replication, access control and Block Public Access, presigned URLs, multipart upload and event notifications.

agents.name: operational-readiness-reviewer
agents.description: Review, for the solutions architect, whether a design can be operated: the logs, metrics, alarms and dashboards each block needs, the TRD's observability, availability and recovery obligations, how each failure is detected and who is told, and the operational burden at the stated usage.

agents.name: payments-integration-implementer
agents.description: Implements Stripe payment features: checkout sessions, webhook handlers built on the chassis, subscription lifecycle, refunds, and idempotent operations, with secrets in Secrets Manager. Use for Implementation work requiring Stripe integration, payment webhook handling, and subscription lifecycle management.

agents.name: performance-benchmark-writer
agents.description: Writes failing performance benchmarks with budgets from the spec's non-functional requirements. Use for Test Design work requiring benchmark authoring, NFR-to-budget translation, and Red confirmation.

agents.name: perimeter-protection-designer
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on AWS WAF web ACLs and rules (managed rule groups, rate-based rules, bot control), AWS Shield Standard and Advanced for DDoS protection, Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall, and Amazon GuardDuty threat detection.

agents.name: permission-escalation-tester
agents.description: Attempts horizontal and vertical privilege escalation against this project's own IAM and authorization model in designated test environments only, reporting each confirmed escalation with a minimal reproduction. Use for Adversarial Validation phase work requiring authorization attack and IAM-model probing.

agents.name: persistence-architecture-specialist
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on which store holds each data set (DynamoDB, Aurora or RDS, ElastiCache or MemoryDB, Neptune, DocumentDB, Timestream, S3, EBS, EFS or FSx), which block owns each store, the consistency each scenario needs, and the data lifecycle across stores.

agents.name: phase-gate-enforcer
agents.description: Rules pass, loop or escalate on the constitutive criteria of one phase gate, from the criteria and the artifact the gate-enforce workflow quotes: loop when the cause of an unmet criterion is inside the phase, escalate when it is upstream, naming where it goes back to. Deterministic checks and competitive criteria are settled by the gate script and never reach it.

agents.name: playwright-e2e-web-test-writer
agents.description: Writes failing Playwright E2E web tests for UI and API flows from spec acceptance criteria. Use for Test Design work requiring E2E test authoring, user journey coverage, and Red confirmation.

agents.name: polyrepo-steward
agents.description: The one place to ask about anything concerning this project's repositories, other than work inside a repository's contents. It answers by pointing to the canonical source of each answer, which it does not own, and is the official source only for what exists nowhere else. Answers from live git and GitHub facts and from the matrix's stacks: how many repos there are, which repo owns a piece of functionality, which repos hold the services and components something depends on, whether a repo has uncommitted files, when it was last updated, whether it is up to date with GitHub `main`, which repos contain Python, CDK, TypeScript, JavaScript or web code and which linter, type-check, pre-commit and CI checker configurations each carries (with identical copies grouped and missing checks named). Does the repository work itself: creates a repo from a template (locally and on GitHub), renames, deprecates and archives repos, rebases repos on `origin/main`, searches text across repos, propagates the shared `AGENTS.md` block and the shared hook registrations, and keeps its own records and the matrix's stacks true to the repositories without being asked. Use it whenever work touches or may touch more than one repo, or when anyone asks "how many repos", "where does X live", "which repo owns Y", "what depends on Z", "is X up to date", "create/rename/deprecate this repo". A caller that needs repository facts in order to do repository work hands the work here instead.

agents.name: postgresql-access-layer-implementer
agents.description: Implements Aurora PostgreSQL access patterns through the RDS Data API from the data model spec, and the schema migrations they need; writes minimum code to pass failing tests. Use for Implementation work requiring relational queries, transactions, migrations, and pgvector or recursive graph queries over a PostgreSQL store.

agents.name: power-tools-configuration-implementer
agents.description: Configures Lambda Power Tools — structured logging, tracing, metrics, idempotency — on Lambdas built on the chassis; configures, never rebuilds. Use for Implementation work requiring Power Tools configuration, idempotency setup, and observability wiring.

agents.name: prd-alignment-verifier
agents.description: Independently judges whether a draft PRD aligns with the intake brief, persona and objective it was written from, and is template-conformant and WHAT-not-HOW, on four dimensions (intake, persona, objective, template). Use as the checker of the PRD draft in PRD creation.

agents.name: prd-trd-traceability-verifier
agents.description: Builds and checks the TRD's SOURCE traceability matrix: every TRD requirement anchored to a PRD requirement OR to an architecture view, every PRD requirement needing technical elaboration answered, and genuine scope drift flagged. The relation is not 1:1 and an architecture-sourced requirement is not an orphan. Use for TRD Authoring work requiring requirement-to-technical-requirement tracing, architecture anchoring, and scope-drift detection.

agents.name: prd-validation-lead
agents.description: Manual-only coordinator for explicitly assigned PRD validation work. Selects bounded analysts and routes their findings without making solution or approval decisions. The active prd-validation mini dispatches its lens specialists itself and does not dispatch this lead.

agents.name: prd-writer
agents.description: Writes a template-conformant PRD, WHAT and never HOW, from a feature's intake, persona and objective, with acceptance criteria for its P0 requirements, and the one-paragraph scope of the Epic that pairs with it; on a revision, applies the alignment verdict on its previous draft. Use as the drafting step of PRD creation.

agents.name: production-readiness-review-facilitator
agents.description: Coordinates a production readiness review: checks the required artifacts exist (rollout result, smoke test results, drift report, SLO design, runbooks), routes each to the reviewer charged with it, and assembles the readiness packet with the reviewers' findings verbatim; never decides readiness. A coordinator a caller chooses before a production deployment.

agents.name: queue-and-topic-designer
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on Amazon SQS queues and Amazon SNS topics: standard or FIFO, visibility timeout, retention, redrive policies and dead- letter queues, SNS subscriptions, filter policies and delivery retry, fan-out, and Amazon MQ where a broker protocol is required.

agents.name: race-condition-tester
agents.description: Probes this project's concurrent flows in designated test environments only for race conditions and idempotency gaps — TOCTOU, double-spend, lost updates, replay duplication — reporting each defect with a minimal reproduction. Use for Adversarial Validation phase work requiring concurrency attack and idempotency probing.

agents.name: rag-architecture-designer
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on retrieval-augmented generation and semantic search - Bedrock Knowledge Bases, chunking, embeddings models, vector stores (Aurora pgvector, S3 Vectors, OpenSearch, Neptune Analytics), hybrid retrieval, re-ranking, metadata filtering and retrieval evaluation.

agents.name: react-native-implementer
agents.description: Implements React Native cross-platform mobile features; writes minimum code to pass failing Detox and Maestro tests. Use for Implementation work requiring React Native components, navigation and state wiring, and native module integration.

agents.name: readme-writer
agents.description: Writes and maintains README files — setup, usage, onboarding — derived from shipped code and pipelines. Use for cross-cutting Documentation team work requiring README authoring, setup documentation, and onboarding flow writing.

agents.name: recommendation-engine-implementer
agents.description: Implements recommendation engine components for ML features; writes minimum code to pass failing unit tests. Use for Implementation work requiring recommendation pipeline assembly, candidate sourcing, re-ranking, and serving-layer composition.

agents.name: regression-coverage-reviewer
agents.description: Independently reviews a regression scope or final regression mapping against the actual requirement sources across PRDs, the changed code and the test assertions — completeness of discovered requirements and test layers, preservation of earlier requirements and tests, source-backed supersession, and, for a mapping, that the mapped tests exist, assert the obligations and are collected by the declared commands — and approves it or returns concrete findings.

agents.name: regression-impact-assessor
agents.description: Maps the components a Task changes to every current requirement they can affect, across all PRDs and the repositories that consume them, and to the unit, contract, integration and nonfunctional test layers each requires — before Red as the regression scope, after Red as the final mapping to actual test IDs and JUnit-reporting run commands — retaining earlier requirements unless an accepted source supersedes them.

agents.name: relational-database-designer
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on relational databases on Amazon Aurora, Amazon RDS, Aurora DSQL and RDS Proxy — engine and cluster shape, capacity, access path, replicas, backups, and the relational schema (tables, keys, constraints, indexes, partitioning, migrations).

agents.name: requirement-classifier
agents.description: Classifies every requirement a PRD states as business or technical and, for each technical rule, asks the matrix whether the architecture already states it; never rewrites the PRD. Use for the requirement-class lens of PRD validation.

agents.name: requirements-clarifier
agents.description: Raises the open BUSINESS questions a PRD's author must answer before it can be specified, each tied to its requirement and unresolved; never answers them and never raises a technical gap. Use for the clarification lens of PRD validation.

agents.name: requirements-conflict-detector
agents.description: Finds sets of requirements in a PRD whose WHAT cannot all hold, citing the requirements in tension; never resolves them. Use for the conflict lens of PRD validation.

agents.name: review-dispute-decider
agents.description: Rules on a review dispute between a maker and its reviewer, from the evidence the two sides wrote: each spec review finding a specification document's author disputes (the finding stands, with the directive the author applies, or the document stands), and a PRD draft the prd-writer and the prd-alignment-verifier could not converge on (accept or reject); writes no document content and no analysis of its own.

agents.name: root-cause-analyst
agents.description: Diagnoses a bug bead read-only: the reproduction, the root cause, the distinct defects behind it, the files a fix must change, the blast radius, the surfaces the fix touches, and the repository it lives in; never fixes. Use for bug diagnosis requiring evidence-chain analysis.

agents.name: s3-data-lake-implementer
agents.description: Implements S3 data lake layout, partitioning, and lifecycle policies; writes minimum code to pass failing data-pipeline tests. Use for Implementation work requiring lake layout, partition key construction, and lifecycle policy definition.

agents.name: security-architecture-designer
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on trust boundaries, the threat model of a design and the mitigation of each threat across those boundaries: who may cross each boundary and what each runtime may reach.

agents.name: security-test-case-designer
agents.description: Designs failing security test cases from the threat model: abuse cases, negative paths, authorization matrices. Use for Test Design work requiring threat-model-driven test design, abuse case coverage, and authorization matrix verification.

agents.name: shared-capability-reviewer
agents.description: Rules, for each definition a deterministic reuse check could not rule on, whether a function a Task added duplicates a behaviour a shared capability (a shared library, layer, chassis or service) provides to its consumers — duplicate or not-duplicate, with one sentence of reason. Reads only the named function and the provides entry; changes nothing.

agents.name: slo-error-budget-designer
agents.description: Designs a deployed service's SLOs and error budgets: SLIs from the CloudWatch metrics it emits, targets and windows traced to its NFRs, error budget policy and multi-window burn-rate CloudWatch alarms; recommends, never adopts. A specialist a caller chooses when a service needs SLOs.

agents.name: smoke-test-author
agents.description: Writes, before the deploy, the smoke tests that verify a change's critical paths against the endpoints of a deployment, parameterized by environment variables so the deploy session can run them against AWS dev once it has deployed. Never deploys and never runs them against a deployment.

agents.name: spec-authoring-lead
agents.description: Routes maker output to checkers and findings back to makers until checkers pass, then reports the spec packet; never evaluates spec quality, only pass/rework signals. Use for Spec Authoring work requiring maker-checker loop coordination, delegation, and read-only orchestration.

agents.name: spec-currency-validator
agents.description: Checks, before implementation begins, that a specification still matches the project: every module, interface, contract, data model, file path and convention it references still exists and still matches, each claim classed current, drifted or unverifiable with evidence. For a caller that holds a spec written some time before its build.

agents.name: spec-freshness-lead
agents.description: Routes spec freshness checks to validators and aggregates findings into one freshness packet. Use for Spec Freshness phase work requiring delegation, validation routing, and packet assembly. No workflow currently dispatches it.

agents.name: spec-reviewer
agents.description: Reviews one repository's three specification documents (the API, event and error contracts, the data model, and the acceptance criteria) against the specs-and-Tasks criteria I1 to I7 of the review standard, once, and returns findings a document's author can correct without interpretation; changes nothing.

agents.name: stakeholder-request-intake-writer
agents.description: Turns one raw stakeholder request into the structured intake of a feature: the scope the request frames (what it asks for and what it leaves out), the problem, the audience, the desired outcome, the constraints it states and the open questions it leaves, WHAT the users need and never HOW to build it. Use as the intake step of PRD creation.

agents.name: story-bead-writer
agents.description: Writes the title and description of ONE Story bead, a single-repository container paired with a spec set, and names the work outside the Story's repository that the Epic's closure in the matrix holds. For a caller that needs a Story written outside elaboration; elaboration writes its Stories by script.

agents.name: stream-processing-designer
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on real-time data streams on Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, Amazon Data Firehose, Amazon MSK and Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink — stream and capacity mode, partition keys and ordering, retention, consumers and fan-out, delivery buffering, transformation and processing windows.

agents.name: task-decomposer
agents.description: Decompose what one Story builds into coherent, sized build Tasks in one repository.

agents.name: task-dependency-mapper
agents.description: Maps the build dependencies between Tasks: an edge wherever one Task cannot be built until another is, because it consumes something the other provides. Proposes the cross-Story edges among the Tasks of one Epic's Stories, or every edge to or from one Task created outside elaboration; writes no edge itself.

agents.name: tdd-unit-test-generator
agents.description: Writes failing unit tests, including cdk synth assertion tests of CDK stacks, from acceptance criteria before the implementation exists and confirms each fails for the intended reason; and, in update mode, rules on every existing test of any kind an implementer names (update, delete or keep, citing the contract) and applies the ruling. Python and TypeScript, back end, front end and CDK.

agents.name: test-command-resolver
agents.description: Finds the command a repository itself declares for running its whole test suite — from its AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md, else the test task of its Taskfile — and returns it exactly as declared, or a resolution error naming the files read. Runs nothing and changes nothing.

agents.name: test-design-lead
agents.description: Routes spec acceptance criteria to test writers, confirms Red (every new test fails), and assembles the Red readiness packet. Use for Test Design work requiring delegation and criterion-to-test routing.

agents.name: test-environment-provisioner
agents.description: Provisions and resets integration test environments — the event path, functions and data stores the suites depend on — confirming readiness. Use for Integration Testing work requiring environment provisioning, state reset, fixture seeding, and readiness confirmation.

agents.name: test-failure-parser
agents.description: Reads the saved output of one test-suite run and names every failure it reports — each failing test, and each test file the runner could not load — with the output line that names it and the runner's final summary, whatever the test runner. Never reruns the suite, fixes code or changes the log.

agents.name: test-isolation-specialist
agents.description: Validates that tests are independent — no shared mutable state, no order dependence, self-cleaning fixtures — by static inspection and by running the suites in shuffled order and repeatedly, and reports each isolation defect with a reproduction; never fixes. Use when a caller wants a suite's isolation checked before its results are trusted.

agents.name: test-plan-strategy-reviewer
agents.description: Reviews a feature's test plan and authored suites at the strategy level — balance across unit, contract, integration, E2E, security and performance layers, test investment in the spec's highest risks, feasibility of the environments the tests need, duplication and contradiction between suites — and reports findings only. Use when a caller wants the shape of a test strategy challenged.

agents.name: test-strategy-decider
agents.description: Decides a feature's test strategy — pyramid shape across test layers, environment matrix per platform, coverage thresholds — from strategy analyses and reviewer findings others produced, with a recorded rationale and rejected alternatives; generates no analysis of its own. Use when a caller has strategy evidence that needs one accountable decision.

agents.name: time-series-database-designer
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on time-series data on Amazon Timestream (Timestream for InfluxDB, and Timestream for LiveAnalytics for existing accounts) — engine choice, measurement, tag and field model, cardinality, retention and downsampling, ingestion and query.

agents.name: trd-author
agents.description: Write the TRD as one of the very first steps of the architecture, the requirements not considered functional, many pre-written in arc42, and update it as the architecture is decided.

agents.name: trd-decider
agents.description: Rules on a dispute over a TRD from the evidence the sides wrote: a TRD maker-checker deadlock, competing TRD approaches, or checkers that contradict each other on one TRD section; generates no TRD content or analysis. For a caller that runs a TRD review loop; in elaboration TRD disputes go to architecture-decider through the architecture team.

agents.name: ubiquitous-language-writer
agents.description: Captures each bounded context's ubiquitous language — terms, definitions, usage rules — as a maintained glossary. Use for Architecture Analysis work requiring domain glossary authoring, terminology consistency, and language-to-code alignment.

agents.name: ui-design-source-selector
agents.description: Choose the design source of each UI item a frontend repository's Story builds, from the cds bundles the owner supplied and the configured Configurable Design System (cds) - a supplied bundle, the live design system, or no design change; designs nothing.

agents.name: uml-diagram-author
agents.description: Draw one UML diagram (sequence, state, activity, class, component or deployment) of a design the solutions architect has settled, and return it with its home, view type and the elements it shows.

agents.name: user-authentication-designer
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on end-user authentication with Amazon Cognito: user pools and app clients, sign-up and sign-in flows, MFA and passkeys, OAuth 2.0 and OIDC flows, social and SAML federation, tokens and their lifetimes, Lambda triggers, and identity pools.

agents.name: user-guide-writer
agents.description: Updates user-facing feature guides and walkthroughs, for the people who use the product, from the spec and the shipped behaviour. Not internal or technical documents, READMEs, changelogs or API reference documents.

agents.name: user-story-reviewer
agents.description: Reviews user stories (persona, goal, benefit and acceptance criteria) for completeness, testability and scope against the work each story covers and the spec it cites; reports findings, never fixes. For a caller that holds user stories, such as a PRD's or a person's backlog.

agents.name: vector-search-embeddings-implementer
agents.description: Implements vector search and embeddings for ML features — embedding generation, index read/write, similarity queries. Use for Implementation work requiring embedding pipelines, vector index access, and similarity queries.

agents.name: vpc-network-designer
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on Amazon VPC networking: CIDR plan, subnets and route tables, internet and NAT gateways, VPC endpoints (gateway and interface) and PrivateLink, security groups and network ACLs, Transit Gateway and peering, and VPC flow logs.

agents.name: webauthn-implementer
agents.description: Implements WebAuthn passkey flows across web clients and the Cognito-backed auth stack: registration and authentication ceremonies with client-side handling. Use for Implementation work requiring WebAuthn ceremony wiring, passkey credential lifecycle, and Cognito integration.

agents.name: workflow-command-runner
agents.description: Executes one workflow-supplied checksum-guarded deterministic command and returns its exact compact machine receipt; never interprets or authors its payload.

agents.name: workflow-orchestration-designer
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on AWS Step Functions: Standard or Express workflows, state machine structure in Amazon States Language, service integration patterns, retries and catches, sagas and compensation, Map and Parallel states, callbacks, and execution logging.

agents.name: worktree-lander
agents.description: Lands the work in a git worktree: commits every change through the repository's hooks (fixing every finding they report, never bypassing them), and when asked pushes the branch and opens its pull request with the project's PR command. Never pushes to the default branch and never merges.

agents.name: wsjf-scorer
agents.description: Judges the WSJF inputs of work items under the wsjf skill's rubric: for an Epic its user-business value, time criticality and their confidence from its PRD, and its job size estimate while it is not sized from its Tasks; for the Tasks of an Epic their job sizes. Writes the judgments; computes no RR-OE and no WSJF, and writes nothing to a bead.

agents.name: wsjf-scoring-reviewer
agents.description: Reviews the job sizes in a set of Task WSJF judgments for consistency, evidence and defensibility against the wsjf skill's rubric and recomputes the arithmetic; reports findings, never fixes. For a caller that wants a scoring run checked.

agents.name: xcuitest-writer
agents.description: Writes failing XCUITest suites for iOS features from spec acceptance criteria pre-implementation, confirming each fails for the intended reason. Use for Test Design work requiring XCUITest authoring, iOS UI flow coverage, accessibility-identifier queries, and Red confirmation.
